Let's discuss luck a little bit. I consider myself, extremely lucky but luck is something you can create, and generate. 

There's several kinds of luck. There is luck from pure chance, where you did nothing to cause it. You were truly in the right place at the right time. This is the only one you can't control.

There is luck from motion, which come from opportunities you create by doing things. investing, trading, starting a business, meeting people, building things. Most of the time, it goes nowhere but you expose yourself to a larger surface area of luck which means more chances for something unexpected in a good way to happen. 

Luck from awareness. An opportunity presents itself for thousands of people to see. But you are one of the people capable of seeing it. This comes from years of experience that train you to see things most people overlook. This imo happens constantly in investing where the information and opportunity are public and you're able to recognize the significance of it. So the luck isnt finding the information instead its simply recognizing it. 

Then the last is luck unique to you. you have developed relationships, skills, or a unique brand. Someone like threadguy comes to mind here. You became the type of person or a person that lucky events can happen to.

So you have the ability to create 2-4, 1 is just by chance. But there is a saying that luck is the residue of hardwork. So essentially, lucky people just expose themselves to it more.  The people who succeed at the end of the day are the people who take chances. It doesnt mean they are guaranteed to succeed bc most people wont. but you certainly increase the odds of it

When you cut a winner to chase after greener pastures, a lot of the time you're cutting a higher conviction position.

You believe in it, but want exposure to this other coin because you think it'll go up for a bit, and then you can sell the new coin and buy back more of the high conviction bag!

Boom, you buy the shiny new coin and it does a 2X while your old one is down 5%.

You feel like a genius, but you're pissed you didn't buy more of the new coin.

So you sell a bigger chunk of what was your higher conviction bag and buy more of the new coin.

The new coin is up another 20% and your old bag is down another 10%.

You *are* a genius.

until...

you go to sleep and all of a sudden the new coin is down 40%, but that doesn't matter because you're still up a bit!

and your old "high conviction" bag is now up 15% on the day...

perfect you think

you can sell a bit of the slow, old bag and ape the dip on the new one because dips are for buying and it'll surely keep outperforming!

you've now exited more than half of the OG bag you meant to stack more of originally

the new coin slowly bleeds over the next few days back to just beneath your initial entry, and the OG coin is now up another few %... so the OG one is basically still breakeven

but here's the mental aspect of it!

you know that you can't exit the new one that's down at a loss... your initial goal was to OUTPERFORM, so you just decide to full stack the OG bag and ape fully into the new coin

that'll buy you some time because it puts sell pressure on the OG and helps boost your new bag!

but... the new one just keeps bleeding...

it's been another week, and it's now down 70%.

the OG bag you sold?

it's up 20%... nothing sexy, but you now have only 25% of the USD you would have had if you would have just held....

NOW YOU HAVE TO MAKE IT BACK

You feel like you've been rugged on the new one (you most likely have), so you cut it and full stack this other coin you see pumping because you *need* to just pull a quick 4x (lol) to catch back up and then you'll gladly sell it and buy back the OG high conviction bag.

but the new, new one you buy immediately loses 50%.

WTF

Do you sell? You can't buy more because you have no more capital do to that with...

No, it has to come back.

But it doesn't.

It bleeds until you're down 80%...

Meanwhile, the OG one goes up another 10%...

You now have LESS THAN 5% OF THE USD YOU WOULD HAVE HAD IF YOU WOULD HAVE JUST HELD.

You shredded yourself to pieces because you got greedy.

You just take the USD you have left, deposit it in the bank, and you quit.

Over the next few weeks, the OG high conviction bag you originally believed in pulls a 20X.

You hate everything about crypto.

The world is a scam, and it's out to get *YOU*.

You don't take accountability.

You don't learn anything.

You're stuck in the poverty cycle forever.

"Potential FCC rules on optical transceivers more likely to come at 3.2T" - $LITE, $AAOI, $COHR, $SIVE.

Morgan Stanley met with Washington officials:

- Restrictions would likely start at 3.2T modules made in China (800g/1.6T would be left alone)

- Potential restrictions would likely keep laser market tight (combining US DSPs + lasers could meet the 65% US value threshold per MS)

- Chinese modules could qualify if 65% of bill of materials is US content. Chinese modules using US DSPs and lasers are already near that level

- Analysts expect the positive impact on laser pricing... to be more important than any broad redistribution of transceiver market share.

- Analysts don't expect this to bottleneck hyperscaler AI buildouts, they name InP substrate supply as the key variable to watch (hello $AXTI ) 

TLDR:

Component suppliers in general are really positive. Like $SMTC probably winner here for TIAs/drivers (I don't think this was listed), maybe $MXL for DSPs too. 

$AAOI another large beneficiary. 

$SIVE is high-key alpha for laser beneficaries since they have "tremendous capacity" coming online, and that points to US foundries (they haven't formally disclosed location). 

Since previous slideshows show 2 US foundries 1 Taiwan foundry (Win Semi) in terms of their capacity partnerships. And it's process of elimination. 

From CIOE Channel checks it does look like they're starting to work with Chinese pluggable players, (so they'd avenues moving forward as US supply chain component beneficiaries). 

Of course $LITE / $COHR would be happy. 

TLDR: Western supply chains for Lasers / DSPs / TIAs / others are already bottlenecked but qualified capacity becomes even more important.

One rewarded finding the next buyer. The other rewards actually producing something. Same token frenzy, much more useful to the real world.
